strategy_plan.planning_summary: The problem requires optimizing a two-layer antireflection coating with fixed materials (SiO2, TiO2) and fixed layer count (one of each). The primary design axes are the discrete choice of layer ordering (SiO2-first vs. TiO2-first) and the continuous optimization of the two layer thicknesses within the [40, 160] nm bounds. Since the maximum number of routes allowed is 1, and the layer order is a discrete binary choice that fundamentally changes the interference physics, the single route must fix one ordering to allow the optimizer to tune the thicknesses effectively. The chosen axis tests the hypothesis that placing the high-index TiO2 layer adjacent to the glass substrate (Air/SiO2/TiO2/Glass) yields a lower mean reflectance than the reverse, as this ordering better matches the impedance gradient from air to glass for broadband suppression. If this specific topology fails to meet the target, the discrete variable (order) would need to be swapped in a subsequent manual iteration, but within the constraints of a single parallel route, we must commit to the physically most promising configuration derived from quarter-wave stack theory adapted for broadband minimization.

# TMM research and design result

Run status: completed. Acceptance: accepted.

## Problem interpretation

Design a planar two-layer antireflection coating on a semi-infinite glass substrate (refractive index 1.52, lossless) with air incidence (index 1.0). The stack must consist of exactly one layer of SiO2 (n=1.46) and one layer of TiO2 (n=2.40) in either order, with each layer thickness constrained between 40 and 160 nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence over the wavelength range 450 to 700 nm (sampled every 5 nm). A mean reflectance below 0.03 is a stated soft target preference. The method must use deterministic Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) only, excluding RCWA, FDFD, surrogates, or hardware acceleration. The optimization allows up to two research rounds with one route and a maximum of 64 solver evaluations per round using seed 17. Final validation requires observing the full spectrum and performing an independent numeric check before claiming the target is met.
